verses.1: And Abraham gathered together his people, and he took a wife named Keturah.
verses.2: And she gave birth to Zimran, Yaqshan, Madian, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuh.
verses.3: And Yaqshan had sons named Shaba and Dedan. Dedan’s sons were Ashurim, Lutushim, and Ummim.
verses.4: And the sons of Midian were Eufa, Epha, Hanoch, Abidah, and Elda’ah. All these were sons of Keturah.
verses.5: And Abraham gave everything he had to Isaac.
verses.6: And the Philistines, who were enemies of Abraham. Abraham gave them gifts, and he sent them away from Isaac’s side, before Isaac was born. They went to a land that was far away from us.
verses.7: And these are the years of Abraham’s life: he lived for one hundred seventy-five years.
verses.8: And Abraham died in good health, as a old man and full of years. He was gathered to his people.
verses.9: And Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the valley of Makpela, in the field of Efrôn, son of Zachar, the priest. This place is located on the banks of Mamre.
verses.10: The land that Abraham bought from the sons of Heth was given to Abraham and his wife Sarah.
verses.11: After Abraham’s death, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac then settled in Beer-Lachai.
verses.12: And these are the daughters of Ismael, son of Abraham. They were born to Abraham from the Egyptian woman Sarah.
verses.13: And these are the names of the sons of Ismael: in the names of their mothers, they were given these names by Ismael himself. They were prophets, kings, and rulers.
verses.14: And it hears, and it resembles, and it carries.
verses.15: He will make it clear and define what is true and what is false.
verses.16: These are the sons of Ismael. Their names are recorded in their palaces and fortresses. There were twenty-two kings who ruled over them.
verses.17: And these two generations of the people of Israel lasted for thirty-three years, seven years, and then they died. They were then gathered together with their people.
verses.18: And they settled from Hivla until Shur, which is on the banks of Egypt. Then Assyria came upon them, and all their brothers were destroyed.
verses.19: And these are the sons of Isaac, son of Abraham. Abraham gave birth to Isaac.
verses.20: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Amorite, from Padan Aram as his wife.
verses.21: Isaac pleaded with Jehovah to have his wife back, as she was barren. Jehovah agreed to this request, and Rebekah’s wife was able to have children again.
verses.22: And the trees were shaken in fear. She said, “If so, then why am I here? Go and seek Jehovah.”
verses.23: And the LORD said to her, “Two nations will be in your womb. Two gods will also be from your womb. They will separate from each other. And the young man will serve the old man.”
verses.24: And her days were filled with childbirth. And behold, she gave birth to a son.
verses.25: And Admoni went out first. He was like a door that opened. They called out his name, “Esho.”
verses.26: And after that, his brothers went out. His hand was holding onto Esau’s arm. They called out his name: Yaakov. Isaac was the son of Shishakiah, who was sixty years old at the time they were being born.
verses.27: And the boys grew up. Esau became a man who knew how to tend the fields, while Jacob became a man who lived in tents.
verses.28: And Isaac loved Esau, because he spoke with him in a friendly manner. And Rebekah also loved Jacob.
verses.29: And Jacob became angry. Esau came out of the field, and he was furious.
verses.30: And Esau said to Jacob, “Come here, I want to speak with you. This man is such a fool; I’m tired of him. So, call him Adam.”
verses.31: And Jacob said, “As surely as I swear today, I will take your daughter for myself.”
verses.32: And Esau said, “Look, I am going to death. Why do you give me this as a gift?”
verses.33: And Jacob said, “Give me seven years.” So he gave him seven years. Then he sold his property to Jacob.
verses.34: And Jacob gave Esau bread and some dried figs. Esau ate, sat down, got up, and went away. Then Esau trampled the grain in his hands.
